LESSON: SELF-CONTROL

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Church
Topic 5.6: Self-control

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Self-control. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why should you practice self- control?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. ractice self-control as guided in Galatians 5:23- 25,
2. make right decisions that are guided by the Holy Spirit,
3. demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body,
4. live Godly lives guided by the Holy Spirit. The learner is guided to: portray self-control’ their day-to- day lives, engaging in sex, watching ungodly movies, drug use and abuse bodies, Galatians 5:23-25. Why should you practice self- control?

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. ractice self-control as guided in Galatians 5:23- 25,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to ractice self-control as guided in Galatians 5:23- 25,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. make right decisions that are guided by the Holy Spirit,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to make right decisions that are guided by the Holy Spirit,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. live Godly lives guided by the Holy Spirit. The learner is guided to: portray self-control’ their day-to- day lives, engaging in sex, watching ungodly movies, drug use and abuse bodies, Galatians 5:23-25. Why should you practice self- control?

Why should you practice self- control?. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Self-control.
2. Explain Self-control to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: read Galatians 5:23-25,
4. Show that you can: ractice self-control as guided in Galatians 5:23- 25,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Self-control. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why should you practice self- control?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read Galatians 5:23-25,
2. In groups, list choices they make in their day-to- day lives,
3. List things that can defile them e.g. engaging in sex, watching ungodly movies, drug use and abuse

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. ractice self-control as guided in Galatians 5:23- 25,
2. make right decisions that are guided by the Holy Spirit,
3. demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body,
4. live Godly lives guided by the Holy Spirit. The learner is guided to: portray self-control’ their day-to- day lives, engaging in sex, watching ungodly movies, drug use and abuse bodies, Galatians 5:23-25. Why should you practice self- control?

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
